CheckTitle: Snowflake accounts federate authentication through SSO
Description: This check verifies that the account has a **SAML2 or External OAuth security integration** configured, so human access is governed by the corporate identity provider rather than by Snowflake-local passwords.
Risk: Snowflake-local passwords sit outside the controls your identity provider applies — **no conditional access, no device posture, no central session revocation**, and no automatic disablement when someone leaves. During an incident, the inability to revoke access centrally materially extends the time an attacker keeps a working credential.

Code.CLI:
CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION corporate_sso
  TYPE = SAML2
  ENABLED = TRUE
  SAML2_ISSUER = 'https://idp.example.com'
  SAML2_SSO_URL = 'https://idp.example.com/sso/saml'
  SAML2_PROVIDER = 'CUSTOM'
  SAML2_X509_CERT = '<certificate>';
Code.Other:
1. Register Snowflake as an application in your identity provider
2. Create a SAML2 (or External OAuth) security integration in Snowflake
3. Test federated login with a pilot user before broad rollout
4. Add a SCIM integration so user and role provisioning follows the IdP
5. Once federation is proven, remove Snowflake-local passwords from human users
6. Retain one break-glass local administrator with a stored, monitored credential
Code.Terraform:
resource "snowflake_saml_integration" "corporate_sso" {
  name           = "CORPORATE_SSO"
  enabled        = true
  saml2_issuer   = "https://idp.example.com"
  saml2_sso_url  = "https://idp.example.com/sso/saml"
  saml2_provider = "CUSTOM"
  saml2_x509_cert = var.idp_certificate
}

Recommendation.Text: Federate human authentication through SAML2 or External OAuth, add SCIM for provisioning, then remove local passwords — keeping one monitored break-glass administrator.
